title: FlowTime: Towards Continuous Generative Watch Time Prediction via Flow-based Personalized Priors

problem.claim: Watch time prediction is important for optimizing deep user engagement in short-video recommender systems.

gap.claim: Existing watch time prediction methods have paradigm-specific limitations and fail to capture the intrinsic multimodality and heterogeneity of user-item interaction patterns.

contributions.claim: The paper presents FlowTime, a method positioned toward continuous generative watch time prediction using flow-based personalized priors.

The proposed direction targets limitations associated with mean-collapse, quantization errors, high inference latency, heuristic vocabulary design, and insufficient modeling of multimodality and heterogeneity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Watch time is identified as a pivotal optimization metric for short-video recommender systems.
Current watch time prediction methods are described as having paradigm-specific limitations.
Direct regression, ordinal regression, and discrete generative regression are associated with distinct modeling or efficiency problems.
Across these paradigms, the shared deficiency is inadequate capture of multimodal and heterogeneous user-item interaction patterns.

source_observation.claim: Different watch time prediction paradigms exhibit different failure modes, while also sharing an inability to model multimodal and heterogeneous interactions.

interpretation.claim: A suitable prediction approach may need to address both paradigm-specific operational issues and the underlying distributional complexity of user-item interactions.

application.claim: When designing watch time prediction systems, evaluate distributional expressiveness and inference practicality together.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish that any particular approach resolves all identified limitations.

unknowns: The supplied units do not describe the flow-based model architecture or training procedure.
The supplied units do not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The supplied units do not establish whether the proposed method improves prediction accuracy, latency, or interaction-pattern modeling.
